devon (Support): FYI customer `acme-corp` (platinum) opened an escalation — they say audit events for resource creation/deletion are missing in their SIEM for ~03:00-03:20 UTC today. They attached a manifest and a couple of sample object keys. They see the forwarder returning 200 but downstream index has big gaps.
elaine (Security): Thanks. Can you paste the tenant id + one example S3 object key and the manifest name? Also: did they see any 403s/KMS errors in the raw forwarder logs?
devon (Support): Tenant `acct-789`. Example object: `s3://redwood-audit/2026-03-17/03/part-0003.gz`. Manifest: `manifests/acct-789/2026-03-17-03.manifest.gz`. Customer attached the manifest and says size is non-zero. No obvious 403 in their splunk, just missing events.
arik (Infra): Quick context — we rotated the KMS alias to `redwood-audit-alt` at ~02:58 UTC (scheduled small key rotation). HSM logs show a brief quota stall during rekey (0:02:58-0:03:02). That can cause a race where forwarder uploads a gz container but the envelope key references the old key version and our forwarder instance retries can produce a truncated multipart object in edge cases.
elaine (Security): That sounds like a possible rekey race. If the object uploaded with an envelope referencing v1 and the KMS store only returns v2 immediately after, decryption shows as truncated/corrupt. We should check forwarder logs for `decryption error`, `incorrect header`, or `truncated gzip`.
devon (Support): Customer gave a forwarder snippet: ``ERROR audit-forwarder upload failed part-0003.gz: decrypt failed: key not found for key-id arn:aws:kms:...:alias/redwood-audit:v1`` and also a repeated `PUT Object 200` entries. They said the SIEM connector dropped 1.2k events from that blob.
arik (Infra): Can we get me the object's ETag + size from S3 and the manifest entry? If the object shows expected size but the blob decompressed smaller / parsing fails, that matches a corruption case. I can run `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit --key 2026-03-17/03/part-0003.gz` to confirm.
devon (Support): Pasted head-object: ``{ "ContentLength": 1572864, "ETag": "\"7f3a2b..\"", "Metadata": {"x-redwood-kms-version":"v1"}}`` Customer unpacked locally and got `gzip: unexpected end of file` when trying to gunzip.
elaine (Security): Ok that matches truncated gzip. Action plan: 1) run forwarder replay for that manifest shard (non-blocking to other tenants), 2) if replay fails with KMS decryption, trigger reencrypt-playbook (decrypt+reencrypt using current key material on infra side) and reupload, 3) push to SIEM.
arik (Infra): I can repro locally by fetching the object and simulating the KMS alias state flip. Repro steps I used: ``# repro steps
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit/2026-03-17/03/part-0003.gz ./part-0003.gz
python -c 'import gzip,sys; f=gzip.open("part-0003.gz"); print(f.read(100))'`` It throws `EOFError: Compressed file ended before the end-of-stream marker`. Then I forced a reencrypt job: ``./infra-tools/reencrypt --tenant acct-789 --object part-0003.gz --from-alias redwood-audit:v1 --to-alias redwood-audit`` which rebuilt the envelope and object. After reupload, `gunzip` succeeded and the SIEM connector picked up 1.2k events.
audit-forwarder-bot: playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/reencrypt-replay (steps: validate manifest -> run replay agent -> monitor SIEM ack).
devon (Support): Customer notified. Starting bounded replay now (non-blocking). I'll update them with ETA.
jules (Customer Success): Please include a summary for the customer: cause = KMS alias rotation + short HSM stall caused envelope mismatch -> produced truncated gzip that SIEM skipped; remediation = infra reencrypt + replay. Also add timeframe and what we changed to prevent recurrence.
elaine (Security): Preventive items: add short grace window around alias rotations (30s) to block forwarder uploads or queue them; add detection in forwarder to mark and hold uploads that failed KMS handshake until rotation completes; emit metric `forwarder.kms.rotation_conflict` to alert automatically.
arik (Infra): I'll schedule a patch to add a rotation-lock and a metric in the forwarder. Also adding a one-off backfill job for `acct-789` for March 17 03:00-03:30.
devon (Support): Replay kicked off at 2324001500, current status: started, 0/4 shards complete, expected finish ~4h. Customer asked for compliance evidence — I'll attach the reencrypt logs and post the SIEM ingestion receipts when done.
elaine (Security): Filing a short incident record (INC-2026-03-AUDIT-01) for the KMS rekey race and the missing-export. Assigning postmortem to @arik.
jules (Customer Success): Customer confirmed receipt of interim note and appreciates the quick response :thumbsup:. Keep me in the loop for the final report.
devon (Support): Noted. Closing slack loop for now, will reopen if replay errors or if any manifold failures.
